Distributionally adaptive regression estimator (series expansion)

Source: R/main.R
series_eq_estimate.Rd

Estimates the conditional mean \(m(x_0) = E[Y \mid X = x_0]\) by a weighted combination of series quantile regression estimates at the levels \(\tau_k = k / (K + 1)\), \(k = 1, \dots, K\). Each covariate is expanded in a B-spline basis, conditional quantiles are fitted with quantreg::rq(), and the weights come from the inverse of the estimated asymptotic covariance matrix of the K quantile estimates. K is chosen from K_grid by L-fold cross-validation.

Usage

series_eq_estimate(Y, X, x0, p, degree, c_band = 1, K_grid, L = 5)

Arguments

Y

Numeric response vector of length n.

X

Numeric matrix or data frame of covariates (n x d).

x0

Numeric vector of length d, the target point.

p

Integer, number of equally spaced knot intervals per covariate (p - 1 interior knots).

degree

Integer, degree of the B-spline basis.

c_band

Numeric scalar, the bandwidth constant.

K_grid

Integer vector of candidate numbers of quantiles K.

L

Integer, number of cross-validation folds.

Value

A list with

  • m_hat_series_eq: the estimate of \(m(x_0)\);

  • cov_hat_series_eq: its estimated standard error;

  • m_hat_series_eq_lower, m_hat_series_eq_upper: the 95% confidence interval, m_hat_series_eq -/+ 1.96 * cov_hat_series_eq.

Details

The bandwidth used for the covariance estimate is \(h = c_{band} \, n^{-1/5}\). Cross-validation folds are drawn after set.seed(1), so results are reproducible, but the global random number generator is reset.

References

Dai, S. (2025). Distributionally Adaptive Regression Estimators. Working paper. https://ssrn.com/abstract=5683602

Examples

set.seed(123)
n <- 500
X <- cbind(rnorm(n), rnorm(n))
Y <- as.numeric(0.5 + X %*% c(1, -1) + rt(n, df = 3))  # heavy-tailed errors
res <- series_eq_estimate(Y, X, x0 = c(0, 0), p = 4, degree = 4,
                          K_grid = c(1, 3), L = 2)
#> Warning: some 'x' values beyond boundary knots may cause ill-conditioned bases
#> Warning: some 'x' values beyond boundary knots may cause ill-conditioned bases
#> Warning: some 'x' values beyond boundary knots may cause ill-conditioned bases
res$m_hat_series_eq  # true value is 0.5
#> [1] 0.3585145
